Our circadian rhythms are nearly 24-hour cycles that regulate alertness, hormones, body temperature and digestion. Deep inside the brain, a cluster of nerve cells called the suprachiasmatic nucleus (SCN) acts as the body’s master clock. The fourth major production by Kochi-based Rasa Theatre Collective, Many A Thousand Years attempts to explore the ‘waiting’ that is central to human existence, inspired by Samuel Beckett’s Waiting for Godot. It is written by Aparna Ashok and directed by Rahul Thomas. Rahul plays Mano, a theatre actor who transforms into Hamlet on stage, seeking an answer to the centuries-old question: to be or not to be? Each night, as Mano washes off his makeup and removes his costumes, he is joined by another actor, Gomi, played by Abraham Vadakkan. Day in and day out, Gomi plays Bhima, who, with a swing of his mace, breaks Duryodhana’s thigh in the Mahabharata .
